summary: All six round-1 findings are addressed, and each fix was re-verified independently by mutation rather than taken on trust. The suite grew from 18 to 22 tests; all 22 pass. I built 18 mutants of src/ui/groupOrderUtils.ts and ran the suite against each — all 18 are killed. Critically, the round-1 undetected case is now caught: reimplementing canMoveGroup so it applies the visible-skipping rule to hidden rows (arrow rendered disabled for a legal move) reddens two tests — the new exhaustive agreement test and the new discriminating hidden-row fixture. Its mirror (literal adjacency applied to visible rows — a live arrow that does nothing) reddens five. The formerly vacuous filtered-projection test now dies under the no-op mutant. The hidden-row rule is no longer pinned by a single assertion (dropping the branch now reddens two tests). The downward multi-hidden step-over closes the loop-bound gap: an off-by-one in `i < order.length` is now caught. The new Array.isArray guard is genuinely exercised — removing it reddens the robustness test. src/ui/groupOrderUtils.ts was restored after every mutant; `git diff` and the md5 of the file both confirm it is byte-identical to HEAD. Only one cosmetic carry-over remains: one it-title still drops the possessive from its TDD anchor.

findings.issue: Carry-over from the round-1 minor naming finding, only half addressed. The describe titles were correctly translated to English, but the it-title still reads 'hidden group swaps with its immediate neighbour regardless of that neighbour visibility' while the TDD anchor in the task file (line 93) reads '... regardless of that neighbour's visibility'. A programmatic check of the 15 anchors against the 22 it-titles matches 14 verbatim and misses this one. The behaviour itself is fully covered — this is a traceability nuisance, not a coverage gap: an exact grep for the anchor string returns nothing, so any later automated anchor audit will report a false miss.
findings.recommendation: Restore the apostrophe: rename the test to 'hidden group swaps with its immediate neighbour regardless of that neighbour\'s visibility' (escape the apostrophe, or switch that one title to double quotes / a template literal). No assertion changes.

Mutant M1b (mirror divergence: literal adjacency applied to visible rows) is KILLED with 5 failures. Mutant M17 (moveGroup silently drops hiddenGroups while the predicate keeps it) is KILLED with 8 failures.

implementationChangeReview.change: findSwapIndex -> findSwap returning {from,to}|null, plus an Array.isArray guard on order and hiddenGroups.
implementationChangeReview.assessment: Both changes are covered. The {from,to} shape removes the second indexOf in moveGroup, so the two positions can no longer disagree; mutants that break the swap itself (M2 no-op, M5 splice-instead-of-swap, M6 in-place mutation, M10 no-op returns the same reference) are all killed. The guard is covered by 'neither function throws when the order or the hidden set is not an array' — mutant M7 (guard removed) is killed by exactly that test, so the new defensive code is not untested dead weight.

mutationRun.tool: hand-written harness, one mutant at a time, suite = npx vitest run tests/unit/groupOrderUtils.test.ts
mutationRun.note: The first harness pass reported two false survivors (M5, M10) caused by vitest's mtime-keyed transform cache not seeing same-second rewrites. Re-run with an fsync plus a 1.2s spacing and a unique marker comment per mutant: both are killed. Every result below is from the corrected run, and the two were additionally re-confirmed by hand.
